- **[Critical, `substantive`, UPHELD] Guard-1 strip commit is never pushed before the server-side `gh pr merge --rebase`, so the strip is invisible to GitHub's rebase.** The Guard-1 (Sub-fix 2) block creates a LOCAL worktree commit at `SKILL.md:6863` (`git -C "$WT" commit -m "issue-<N>: strip foreign tasks/ folders before Step-10d merge"`). The safe-case merge at `SKILL.md:7066` (`gh pr merge <PR> --rebase --delete-branch=false`) is server-side: GitHub rebases the commits present on the PR head ref (`origin/issue-<N>`), not the local worktree HEAD. The ONLY `git -C "$WT" push` in the entire file is at `SKILL.md:7110`, inside the merge-conflict RECOVERY sub-procedure that runs ONLY after `gh pr merge` has already been refused (`SKILL.md:7093-7096`, 7117). On the normal success path there is NO push between 6863 and 7066. Therefore the server replays the branch WITHOUT the strip commit and the foreign `tasks/*` reverts/rewinds Guard-1 was built to remove are still present in the replayed history — the exact conflict/revert risk (incident #458 rewinding `tasks/running/448/events.jsonl`) that Sub-fix 2's production path was supposed to eliminate.

**Minor (not blocking, noted):** tests do not assert push-before-merge sequencing — a real coverage gap, but non-blocking on its own.

**Rationale (≤300 words):**
Verified independently against the diff. Three facts, all confirmed by reading `SKILL.md:6840-7117` and grepping every `git -C "$WT" push`:
1. Guard-1 produces a fresh LOCAL commit at line 6863 (idempotent conditional commit of the FOREIGN reset/removal).
2. The safe-case merge at line 7066 is server-side `gh pr merge --rebase`.
3. The only worktree push (line 7110) is recovery-only, reached ONLY after `gh pr merge` is refused — never before the safe-case merge on the success path.

GitHub's `--rebase` replays the PR head ref as it exists on `origin/issue-<N>`; an unpushed local commit cannot participate. So the strip is a no-op with respect to the merge that consumes it — a scaffolded-but-not-plumbed defect: the fix is built but never delivered to the surface the merge reads. Worse, if the server rebase happens to succeed textually, the foreign reverts land on `main` silently (no conflict surfaced), the recovery push is never reached, and Guard-1's protection is defeated exactly where it matters most.

The Claude PASS verified the CONTENT of the Guard-1 split (FOREIGN_ON_MAIN/FOREIGN_BRANCH_ONLY logic, idempotent commit) but never traced the commit's reachability by the server-side rebase — it confirmed the commit is created, not that it reaches the server before the merge depends on it. That is the miss.

The blocker tag is `substantive`, which is NOT in the Step 5c-bis strippable set {`marker-shape`, `smoke-run-missing`, `git-provenance`}, so no mechanical strip applies. Codex was right; Claude was wrong. Fix: push the worktree branch after the guarded strip commit succeeds and before `gh pr merge --rebase` (and add the sequencing assertion the minor item names).
